Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. Afghanistan's head coach has gathered his boys in a huddle for some final instructions before they go out. The two Indian openers wait on the sidelines for the two umpires. Mahboob Khan leads his troops out onto the park. Aaron George and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will open the innings for India. Abdul Aziz will start with the new ball. George will face the first ball from the right-arm quick. A slip in place. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Chase coming up - While India Under-19 have the resources to chase down this daunting total, it will require a collective effort. In their favour is the pitch, which over the 50 overs did not show any signs of changing its behaviour. Afghanistan Under-19, meanwhile, will back themselves to defend the total and carry the advantage of knowing what worked for the Indian bowlers on this surface. They will hope to carry the momentum into their bowling effort. Stay tuned for India's reply.

A quick word with one of the two centurions - Faisal Khan (110 runs off 93 balls) thanks the Almighty. He says that he just wanted to rotate the strike and the ball was coming on nicely. Mentions that before the game, the coach gave them the plan and it was for the openers to play the first 10 overs. Tells that they wanted to take on the bowlers after 40 overs, which they did well. Says that it is a good total on the board, and their bowlers are confident of defending this one.

From platform to power - Faisal's 148-run stand with Uzairullah Niazai was particularly intriguing. While Niazai struggled to find fluency and chewed up a fair number of dot balls, Faisal continued to tick along smoothly at the other end. He remained unfazed by what was happening around him and went on to bring up his second successive century. As the innings progressed, Niazai began to find his rhythm and took it upon himself to ensure the momentum did not dip after Faisal fell and notched up his hundred along the way.

Positive beginning - After opting to bat first, Afghanistan made a steady start through their openers. There was little assistance on offer from the surface or through the air. The Indian bowlers struggled to find consistency, often drifting too full or too short. Khalid Ahmadzai, in particular, was able to capitalise on that inconsistency. They scored 52, 51, and 54 runs across the three 10-over phases in Powerplay 2, and Faisal Khan was the chief architect of their platform.

Excellent finish for Afghanistan Under-19 - 111 runs came in the final 10 overs, which has powered them to an imposing total of 310. As the Indians walk off the park, they look tired and will be disappointed with how the innings finished.

A couple of runs to end the innings! Henil Patel hits the length hard and around middle, Abdul Aziz flat-bats it in the air over the bowler's head but it lands safely. Two taken. The fielder also hits the stumps at the bowler's end, and Niazai thinks about the third, but decides against it. Afghanistan Under-19 finish on 310/4!

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now! The sun is out here in Harare and there is no threat of rain at the moment. Hopefully, it remains the same. We can see the India Under-19 players in a huddle, before they spread out and take their fielding positions. Osman Sadat and Khalid Ahmadzai are the two openers for Afghanistan Under-19. R.S. Ambrish has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Two slips in place as well. Let's play...

We are moments away from the first ball, but before that, Ayush Mhatre and Mahboob Khan lead their respective teams out in the middle and line up for the national anthems. It will be Afghanistan's first, followed by that of India.

A quick chat with India's head coach - Hrishikesh Kanitkar says it has been a great journey so far and believes the boys are talented. He acknowledges that many of them are not yet used to the scale of a stage like this. Kanitkar adds that this is where he feels he can contribute most as a coach. Reckons that for the players, it is about understanding what works for them and continuing to trust that process. He also points out that there will be plenty of distractions, especially external noise, and stresses the importance of not being sidetracked by them. Credits the approachable nature of Sunil Joshi and VVS Laxman for making it easier for young players to open up and settle into the setup.

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawayo is pitchside. He says that there was some rain around to start the World Cup, but Harare has one of the best drainage systems in Zimbabwe, and the outfield has quickened up. Ed Rainsford joins him and says that they are at 1500-metre altitude and the ball is going to fly. Tells that if the batters trust their shots, it will get over. Mentions that the middle overs have been the toughest going at 4.5 runs per over, but you need to push the game on in that phase. Says that the surface looks really hard. A few cracks, but he doesn't expect it to have much impact. Ends by saying that there is some grass covering, he expects it to come on nicely, but as a bowler, you just want the ball in your hand.

The captain of India Under-19 - Ayush Mhatre says that he is happy to bowl first, and it looks like a good wicket. Shares that he is happy with the attitude his boys have shown on the field. Mentions that they want to keep things simple. Informs that they are unchanged for this game.

The captain of Afghanistan Under-19 - Mahboob Khan says that they will bat first. Adds that the wicket looks good for batting. Praises Faisal Khan for the way he has batted throughout the World Cup. Mentions that there is not much difference in the wicket, just it's good for batting and maybe some swing. Ends by saying that they are a very good team and want to make it to the final.

Afghanistan Under-19 (Playing XI) - Khalid Ahmadzai, Osman Sadat, Faisal Khan, Uzairullah Niazai, Mahboob Khan (C/WK), Aziz Mia Khil, Khatir Stanikzai (In for Aqil Khan), Nooristani, Abdul Aziz, Rohullah Arab and Wahid Zadran.

India Under-19 (Unchanged Playing XI) - Aaron George, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ayush Mhatre (C), Vihaan Malhotra, Abhigyan Kundu (WK), Vedant Trivedi, R.S. Ambrish, Kanishk Chouhan, Khilan A. Patel, Henil Patel and D. Deepesh.
TOSS - Ayush Mhatre and Mahboob Khan are all set for the flip of the coin. The coin goes up and comes down in favour of Khan. Afghanistan elect to BAT first.

Afghanistan's tale - For Afghanistan Under-19, this has been a tournament of redemption. After being winless in the group stage in the previous edition in 2024, they have turned the script completely this time, toppling the likes of South Africa and West Indies. This marks Afghanistan's third semi-final appearance in the tournament's history, and they are now eyeing a maiden final in a global event, a first at any level, whether junior or senior. India's story - The five-time champions have not been as dominant as we have come to expect from them at this tournament and have faced challenges along the way from Bangladesh and Pakistan. Ayush Mhatre’s side will be well aware that they have not quite played their best cricket yet, and they will be striving to find that level today, and should the result go their way, once again on the day of the final.

History meets Opportunity - We are down to the second semi-final in the 2026 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup, where two Asian challengers lock horns at the Harare Sports Club. India, the most successful side in men's Under-19 World Cup history with five titles, are eyeing a sixth crown and a sixth successive final. Standing in their way are Afghanistan, chasing not only their maiden title but also a first-ever appearance in an Under-19 World Cup final. Afghanistan's journey so far - Mahboob Khan-led Afghanistan were placed in a tough group alongside South Africa, West Indies, and Tanzania, but they came through it dominantly. They won all three of their matches, topped the group, and carried four points into the Super Six stage. Their only blemish in the tournament came against Sri Lanka, but they bounced back in style. A massive 191-run win in their next outing against Ireland sealed qualification, with Afghanistan finishing second in Group 1, ahead of Sri Lanka on the standings. With the bat, left-hander Faisal Khan has carried the bulk of the scoring. Osman Sadat has also contributed important runs, helping offset an underwhelming campaign from Khalid Ahmadzai. After scoring 74 in the tournament opener, Ahmadzai has managed a highest score of just 34 across the following four matches. Afghanistan are traditionally known for their spin strength, but in this tournament, it has been their pace attack that has done most of the damage. The pacers have picked up 25 wickets so far, compared to 14 by the spinners. Nooristani has spearheaded the pace attack and has been well supported by Khatir Stanikzai and Abdul Aziz. On the spin front, Wahid Zadran and Rohullah Arab may not have many wickets to show, but they have been economical and effective in controlling the game. India's road to the semis - Ayush Mhatre's side is unbeaten in this edition so far. They may have shown a few cracks along the way, but they have still found ways to get the job done. They began their campaign with a win over the USA, followed by a hard-fought victory against Bangladesh, before brushing aside New Zealand to top the group. Zimbabwe were unable to put up much of a fight either, while Pakistan pushed them hard, but India once again managed to come out on top to finish first in Group 2. At the top of the order, India have experimented with their combinations. The first two games saw Ayush Mhatre and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi open, but in the next three matches, Aaron George partnered Sooryavanshi, with Mhatre moving down to number three. That shuffle has not quite paid dividends. Vaibhav has been the lone standout at the top with 196 runs, while both Mhatre and George have only managed double-digit tallies so far. The middle order has come to their rescue, with Abhigyan Kundu, Vihaan Malhotra, and Vedant Trivedi stepping up with timely contributions. With the ball, Henil Patel has stood out, while fellow quick R.S. Ambrish has also shown promise. D. Deepesh, however, is yet to make a mark. Khilan A. Patel has led the spin bowling charge, and India's depth is evident in the number of batting options who can also roll their arm over, with the likes of Malhotra and Mhatre chipping in when required. Form (Last 5 completed youth ODIs, most recent first) - Afghanistan - WLWWW | India - WWWWW. Does anyone have the edge? We don't think so. On paper, India might appear to hold a slight advantage, largely because of the exposure they have had to high-pressure environments in the lead-up to the World Cup. Be it the IPL, various overseas tours, or the domestic circuit, several players in this squad have already been tested in demanding situations. That said, Afghanistan will draw plenty of confidence from their exploits in India last year during the triangular series involving India A and India B. Those Indian sides featured multiple players who are part of the current Under-19 World Cup squad, and Afghanistan won three games out of four matches to qualify for the final, which eventually ended in a no result. With experience on one side and belief on the other, this semi-final promises to be a true contest of temperament, where execution on the day, more than reputation, could decide who books a place in the final.
